what.question: What is Sunrise?
what.answer: Sunrise is a production-ready Next.js starter template designed for rapid application development. It includes authentication, database setup, email integration, Docker deployment, and follows best practices for AI-assisted development.

free.question: Is Sunrise really free?
free.answer: Yes! Sunrise is open source under the MIT License. You can use it for personal and commercial projects without any restrictions. We offer paid support packages for teams that want additional assistance.

technologies.question: What technologies does Sunrise use?
technologies.answer: Sunrise is built with Next.js 16, TypeScript, PostgreSQL with Prisma ORM, better-auth for authentication, Tailwind CSS with shadcn/ui components, React Email with Resend, and Docker for deployment.

aiOptimized.question: How is Sunrise optimized for AI development?
aiOptimized.answer: Two ways. First, AI-assisted development: comprehensive documentation in CLAUDE.md and the .context/ substrate helps AI assistants understand the codebase and follow established patterns when generating code. Second, AI agent capabilities for the apps you build: a complete orchestration layer for designing, deploying, and monitoring AI agents.

agents.question: Can I build AI agents with Sunrise?
agents.answer: Yes. Sunrise ships with a full agent orchestration layer at /admin/orchestration: configure LLM providers, define agents with system instructions and budgets, create custom capabilities (tools), build multi-step workflows as DAGs, ingest documents into pgvector-backed knowledge bases for RAG, expose agents via an MCP server or embed widget, and monitor everything with execution tracing, evaluations, and an audit log. Built on the 21 agentic design patterns from Antonio Gullí.

commercial.question: Can I use Sunrise for commercial projects?
commercial.answer: Absolutely! Sunrise is released under the MIT License, which allows commercial use, modification, and distribution. You just need to include the original license in any copies of the software.

support.question: How do I get support?
support.answer: For free support, you can open issues on GitHub or participate in community discussions. For priority support, architecture reviews, or custom development, check out our Pro Support and Enterprise packages.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.problem: Modern web development involves countless decisions — frameworks, authentication, databases, deployment, testing, and more. Each choice requires research, implementation, and debugging. This takes time away from building the features that matter most.
mission.solution: Sunrise solves this problem by providing a complete, production-ready foundation. We've made the hard decisions, implemented best practices, and documented everything thoroughly. You get a head start measured in weeks, not hours.
mission.agents: And because modern apps increasingly include AI agents, Sunrise ships with a complete orchestration layer too: providers, agents, capabilities, workflows, knowledge bases, and observability. The boring stuff done well — plus the modern agentic primitives so your app can include AI agents from day one.

form.help: Paste an API key from your organisation's own {name} account. Your organisation's calls to {name} then go out on it, and {name} bills that account.
form.helpTest: Before it is saved, the key is tried with one small request to {name}. A key that fails is not saved. Once saved, it is never shown again: only its last four characters are.
form.helpReplace: Saving replaces the current key: this organisation's calls use the new key within a minute. Use this when a key has leaked or you are moving to a new one.
form.failed: The key could not be saved. Try again.

supportAccess.title: Support access
supportAccess.intro: Whether the platform's support staff may work inside this organisation, and for how long.
supportAccess.singleTenant: Support access is for installs with more than one organisation. This install has one.
supportAccess.noOrg: You are not acting in an organisation, so there is nothing to grant.

form.title: Grant support access
form.description: Let the platform's support staff into this organisation for a limited time, to help with a problem. Any of them can enter until the grant ends or you revoke it.
form.durationHelp: Support can enter until this time runs out. Nothing needs doing when it ends: access stops on its own.
form.durationHelpMax: The longest grant is {max}. If support needs longer, grant again with a new reason.
form.reasonHelp: Say what support is helping with, for example a ticket number or the agent that is not working. Support sees this when they enter, and it stays on the record of this grant.
form.replaces: Support already has access. Granting again ends the current grant and starts this one.

grants.empty: Support has never been given access to this organisation.
grants.revokeDescription: Support loses access to this organisation now, including anyone from support who is working in it. You can grant access again at any time.
grants.revokeFailed: Could not revoke support access. Try again.

lists.openFailed: Could not open the list. Try again.

wave.countInvalid: Enter a whole number from 1 to {max, number}.

wave.sendFailed: The invitations could not be sent. Try again.

entries.title: People
entries.loadFailed: The waitlist could not be loaded. Please try again.
entries.searchHelp: Matches the address, the name, or any of the form's answers. The address is matched as you type it; answers are matched exactly as written.
entries.listHelp: Show one list, or every list the app declares.
entries.showUnconfirmedHelp: People who have not clicked the link in their confirmation email. Anyone can type any address into the form, so these are hidden by default and never invited.

user.label: User
user.description: Everyone with an account. Has no platform powers: what they can do inside an organisation comes from their organisation role.

platformAdmin.label: Platform admin
platformAdmin.description: Runs this install for every organisation, from the install org. There it opens every admin page, including the ones kept for the platform, and is not limited by an organisation's switches. Inside a customer's organisation it has only the role that organisation gave it.

support.label: Support access
support.description: A platform admin let into one organisation for a limited time, because its owner agreed. Only an owner can grant it, at full admin or read-only level; an owner or admin can end it at any time.

owner.label: Owner
owner.description: Runs the organisation. Opens every admin page the organisation can use, manages its members and settings, and can grant support access.

admin.label: Admin
admin.description: Helps run the organisation. Opens the same admin pages as an owner, but cannot make anyone an owner, change or remove an owner, or grant support access.

member.label: Member
member.description: Uses the product. Does not open the admin console.

namedTier.description: A role this app adds. Opens only the pages listed for it, in the organisation where it is held.

permissions.platformPages: Open the pages kept for the platform team
